title: Haematuria following a marathon run: source and significance
claims: Urine specimens were obtained from 98 runners before and immediately after running a half marathon (21 km) or full marathon (42 km).
Proteinuria occurred in 35% of those running the half and 69% of those running the full marathon.
Haematuria with or without proteinuria occurred in 21% running the half and 22% running the full marathon.
Among runners with haematuria, dysmorphic erythrocytes were found in 30% of the half-marathon group and 81% of the full-marathon group.
No urinary abnormalities were found on repeat examination 4 to 12 weeks after the run.
The authors concluded that non-glomerular bleeding, possibly from bladder contusions, predominates at shorter distances, while glomerular bleeding occurs with greater distances.
The authors stated that these abnormalities disappear with rest and do not appear to signify underlying urinary tract disease.

claimVerification.note: 前瞻观察 98 名半马/全马跑者，赛前及赛后即刻留尿。
血尿（伴或不伴蛋白尿）半马 21%、全马 22%。
血尿者中畸形红细胞半马 30%、全马 81%。
赛后 4–12 周复查未见尿异常。
作者据畸形红细胞比例推断短距离以非肾小球（可能膀胱挫伤）为主，长距离出现肾小球出血。
作者结论：异常随休息消失，不提示潜在尿路疾病。
